title: NY State Assembly · District 36
area: Queens: Astoria and Long Island City

context.text: The seat became vacant when Zohran Mamdani (D) resigned after being elected Mayor of New York City. Diana Moreno won a February 3, 2026 special election with 74.1% of the vote over Rana Abdelhamid (Queens For All) and Mary Jobaida (People First Party).

In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for a full term, incumbent Diana Moreno defeated Mary Jobaida and Kevin Coenen, winning 78.3% of the vote. The Republican and Working Families Party primaries were canceled; Edward Lee (R) and Moreno (WFP) each advanced without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Diana Moreno
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 36 (since February 2026)

summary.text: Diana Moreno is the incumbent Assembly Member for District 36, elected in a February 2026 special election to succeed Zohran Mamdani after he became mayor. An immigrant-rights and labor organizer, she describes herself as a democratic socialist and is a member of the New York City Democratic Socialists of America. She won the June 2026 Democratic primary and is on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot.

background.text: Moreno was born and raised in Quito, Ecuador, and immigrated to the United States with her family at age 11. According to the Queens Daily Eagle, she spent her early years in the U.S. in Lakeland, Florida.
She holds an associate degree from Santa Fe College and a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida, according to Ballotpedia.

Her official biography says she began as an organizer unionizing faculty and graduate students, protecting the rights of migrant farmworkers and their children, and organizing immigrant workers as an intern for Make the Road New York; the Queens Daily Eagle reports the internship brought her to Queens.

She worked at the immigrant-advocacy group New Immigrant Community Empowerment (NICE) from 2019 to 2023, leaving as its deputy director, according to the Queens Daily Eagle. Her official biography says she organized undocumented workers in Queens against wage theft and advocated for workplace safety legislation for construction workers.

Most recently before the Assembly she worked for the New York State Nurses Association (NYSNA), supporting union nurses and healthcare workers in contract campaigns; the Queens Daily Eagle describes this as communications work.

Moreno joined the Democratic Socialists of America and worked with Mamdani on his 2020 Assembly campaign, according to the Queens Daily Eagle, which reported her 2025 campaign launch as her first run for office. Her official biography also lists volunteer work including starting free English classes at the Astoria Food Pantry.

She won the February 3, 2026 special election with 74.1% of the vote over Rana Abdelhamid (Queens For All) and Mary Jobaida (People First Party), and assumed office on February 4, 2026. On June 23, 2026 she won the Democratic primary for a full term with 78.3%.

She is a member of the Assembly Committees on Aging, Agriculture, Real Property Taxation, Small Business, and Social Services, and of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus, the Legislative Women's Caucus, and the Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.
Her campaign website lists endorsements that include Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the New York City Democratic Socialists of America.
According to her official biography, she became a mother in 2024 and lives in Astoria with her partner and son.

priorities.text: "I am a Queens mom, immigrant, organizer, and the Assemblymember for Astoria and Long Island City. I ran for office to fight for working families and ensure that everyone, regardless of income or background, has the opportunity to thrive."
Universal No-Cost Childcare: "I am fighting for universal no-cost childcare because no parent should have to choose between raising their children and making ends meet."

Protect Immigrants & Abolish ICE: "I support New York For All, ending cooperation between New York State and ICE, and building a future where immigrant families can live safely and thrive without fear."

Tenant Protections & Affordable Housing: "I am fighting for stronger tenant protections, deeply affordable housing, and an affordability agenda that helps working families stay in the communities they helped build."

positions.summary: Campaigns on enacting universal, no-cost childcare for children from six weeks to five years old, funded by taxing high earners.
positions.quote: Work with Mayor Mamdani to tax the rich and fund free childcare for every New Yorker aged six weeks to five years.

positions.summary: Says she will strengthen tenant protections and defend rent stabilization, and supports creating a public Social Housing Development Authority.
positions.quote: Strengthen tenant protections, defend rent stabilization, and create a Social Housing Development Authority to build and preserve affordable housing with union labor.

positions.summary: Opposes expanded immigration enforcement; supports the New York For All Act to restrict state and local cooperation with ICE.
positions.quote: Stand up for our immigrant neighbors under attack from Trump's cruel and racist deportation machine, and pass the New York For All Act to restrict cooperation with ICE.

positions.summary: Supports taxing high earners to fund public childcare and other services.
positions.quote: Work with Mayor Mamdani to tax the rich and fund free childcare for every New Yorker aged six weeks to five years.

record.text: Prime sponsor of A10340-A, which would increase tax rates on unincorporated businesses and corporations in New York City upon adoption of a local law by the City Council. Amended and recommitted to the Ways and Means Committee on 03/23/2026; remains pending.

Sponsor (introduced by Rules on her behalf) of A11289, the "Not on our dime!" act, which would prohibit not-for-profit corporations from providing unauthorized support to Israeli settlement activity and would create a civil penalty and private right of action for violations. Referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee on 05/08/2026; remains pending.

Sponsor (introduced by Rules on her behalf) of A11580, which would increase penalties on gas and electric utilities for failing to file or correct required annual reports with the Public Service Commission. Referred to the Energy Committee on 06/05/2026; remains pending.
Won the February 3, 2026 special election for Assembly District 36 with 74.1% of the vote, succeeding Zohran Mamdani.

candidates.name: Edward Lee

summary.text: Edward Lee is the Republican candidate for Assembly District 36. He describes himself as a longtime independent political activist who has organized cross-partisan candidate forums and debates in New York City.

background.text: Lee says he has been a political activist for over 30 years and, in 2022, 2024, and 2026, gathered candidates across party lines at a project he founded (unifiedplatformusa.com) to document areas of agreement among them.
He says he has organized what he describes as New York City's only third-party and independent candidate debates.
Ballotpedia lists his profession as activist. He is the Republican candidate in 2026; the Republican primary was canceled and he advanced without appearing on the ballot.

priorities.text: Lee's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response focuses on government transparency and accountability and on advocacy work regarding individual cases he says involve wrongful conviction and elder abuse; it does not lay out a conventional legislative platform.
His campaign site says he stands for responsible and reduced government spending, transparency, and "REAL JUSTICE".
priorities.quote: I stand FOR RESPONSIBLE and REDUCED government spending, transparency, and REAL JUSTICE (not funding Not for Profit Executives)

candidates.researchNotes: Sources are his 2026 Ballotpedia survey and campaign site (licgop.com). Neither sets out positions on the guide's issues; his site's remark about Israel concerns its influence on governance, not U.S. aid, so no statement or stance is recorded on that issue.
